headline: Curaleaf UK lab to make and ship Canada's PURPLEFARM medical cannabis
dek: Curaleaf Laboratories will manufacture, pack and distribute PURPLEFARM products in the UK, a day after Boots opened a high-street route to medical cannabis prescriptions.
key_points: Curaleaf Laboratories, Curaleaf's UK manufacturing arm, signed a deal on 17 November 2026 to make, package and distribute PURPLEFARM products for the UK.
PURPLEFARM is a Canadian indoor grower with sites in Ontario and New Brunswick; its products are now available through UK prescribing routes.
The deal is at least Curaleaf Laboratories' fifth UK partnership in about a year, after ANTG, Sanity Group, Herdade das Barrocas and Vericura.
It lands a day after Boots launched SureLeaf, an online specialist medical cannabis service.
body: Curaleaf Laboratories, the UK manufacturing and distribution arm of Curaleaf Holdings, has agreed to manufacture, package and distribute products from Canadian grower PURPLEFARM for the British medical cannabis market. The companies announced the deal on 17 November, according to Business of Cannabis, which carried the announcement.

Under the agreement, PURPLEFARM supplies the cannabis and Curaleaf Laboratories turns it into finished products at its facility licensed by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), then ships them to prescribers and pharmacies across the UK. The companies say PURPLEFARM products are now available through authorised prescribing routes.

PURPLEFARM grows indoors at facilities in Ontario and New Brunswick and sells into regulated international medical markets through pharmaceutical and distribution partners. Its chief executive and co-founder, Mitchell Alswiti, called the deal an important step in its international growth.

Curaleaf Laboratories has been part of Curaleaf International since 2019. It grew out of a specials medicines manufacturer with more than a decade of experience in unlicensed medicines and says it was the first UK manufacturer of full-spectrum medical cannabis. Its own website lists dried flower, oils, vape cartridges, pastilles and suppositories in its range. Managing Director Richard Hodgson said the partnership is meant to widen eligible patients' access to cannabis-based medicines.

The PURPLEFARM agreement is the latest in a run of similar deals. Business of Cannabis lists earlier Curaleaf Laboratories tie-ups with ANTG in November 2025, Sanity Group in February 2026, Portugal's Herdade das Barrocas in June 2026 and Vericura in October 2026. Our count: that is at least five foreign or brand partners routed through one UK plant in about a year.

The model is simple. Overseas growers that meet EU-GMP standards still need a UK partner that can manufacture, hold stock and distribute to prescribers. Curaleaf Laboratories, which describes itself as a manufacturer, distributor and partner for licensed producers and cultivators, sells that access. Each new partner adds products to its range without Curaleaf having to grow the plants.
> In the UK, the scarce asset is not cannabis. It is a licensed factory that can turn someone else's flower into a legal prescription.

The deal comes a day after Boots, the UK's largest pharmacy chain, launched SureLeaf through Boots Online Doctor, as we reported on 16 November. SureLeaf offers specialist-led assessments for patients with eligible chronic pain, generalised anxiety disorder or insomnia, with products sent by mail. StratCann reported that a one-month trial with specialist review costs £89 and that flower is listed from £38 for 5 grams. Boots has said it works with UK suppliers growing in the UK.

A mainstream retailer entering the market should lift prescription volumes and make reliable supply more valuable. It also raises the bar for quality and consistency, which is where large pharmaceutical-style manufacturers expect to win. Smaller importers that rely on a single foreign grower face a more crowded shelf.

Supply has been an issue. Business of Cannabis reported on 12 November that the Dutch health minister told parliament that UK supply was under investigation, and that Bedrocan, the long-time Dutch medical cannabis supplier, could be revived under a new entity. As we reported on 14 November, the Dutch government is weighing a Bedrocan restart. Several supply partners give a UK manufacturer more room if any one source is disrupted.

For Curaleaf Holdings, the UK plant is a way to build a medical business under a single national regulator, something its state-by-state US operations cannot offer. Each partnership keeps that plant busier and spreads its fixed costs over more products. The companies did not disclose financial terms for the PURPLEFARM agreement.

Watch how quickly prescriptions grow after Boots' entry, and whether other high-street chains follow. Watch whether Curaleaf Laboratories signs more growers, and whether other UK manufacturers respond with similar deals. And watch the Bedrocan situation in the Netherlands, which could still shift supply into the UK market.
